title: Adapter pattern: this plan consumes the projection, doesn't extend DontPanic
body: All code in this plan lives outside `scripts/dontpanic_orchestrate/`. The boundary: DontPanic emits state via projection (plan 2026-05-09-003); this adapter consumes and renders. If a feature requires DontPanic core changes, that signals scope creep and the change should be pulled into the projection plan instead.

title: Single-tenant Firestore shape — multi-tenant archived
body: The dashboard's existing `tenants/{tenantId}/...` shape was for the deprecated multi-tenant Axiom direction. Per plan 2026-05-03-002 D002, that direction is archived. This plan uses single-tenant `projects/{project_id}/...` where project_id is the operator's local DontPanic project_id from `~/.dontpanic/projects.json`. Multi-tenant orchestration becomes a future plan if real demand emerges.

title: Mutations through MCP only, never direct Firestore writes
body: The dashboard's drag-and-drop, approve-button, and dispatch-button UIs MUST call Cloud Functions that call DontPanic MCP. Direct Firestore writes for state changes are rejected by the security rules (F004). This preserves DontPanic's approval semantics: every state-changing tool requires `confirm: true` and surfaces the operation to the user before firing. Bypassing MCP would let the dashboard change state without operator approval — exactly the safety failure DontPanic exists to prevent.

title: Polling daemon v0; long-poll / SSE in v1
body: V0 uses a 5–15s polling daemon because it's simpler, has no port management on the operator's machine, and is robust to restarts. V1 may switch to `state_stream` long-poll once the projection plan ships streaming semantics. Polling latency target ≤30s is acceptable for kanban use; sub-second latency isn't a v0 requirement.

title: Local MCP exposure to Cloud Functions: operator's choice
body: Cloud Functions calling DontPanic MCP need a network path to the operator's local machine. Recommended: Tailscale Funnel (encrypted, identity-aware, no port-forward management). Alternatives: Cloudflare Tunnel, ngrok with auth. Operator picks; F003 documents but doesn't enforce. The daemon-vs-Functions split keeps DontPanic itself unaware of any of this — DontPanic just exposes MCP locally.

title: Plan renamed from feat-team-dashboard-sync to feat-firebase-dashboard-adapter-v0
body: Original framing ("team dashboard sync") implied the dashboard itself was the deliverable here. Verification on 2026-05-10 corrected that: DontPanic already ships a local-first static dashboard at DontPanic/dashboard/ that consumes JSON files. The static dashboard moves into plan 2026-05-09-003 F007 (it's OSS-friendly and works without Firebase). THIS plan is now the OPTIONAL realtime/team upgrade — Firebase Auth + Firestore onSnapshot listeners + Cloud Functions for drag-flip mutations. The static dashboard from plan 003 F007 is the prerequisite; this adapter layers realtime ON TOP. The directory was renamed (git mv) since the plan is still status:draft. F001/F002/F003/F005 acceptance updated to reflect the static-first-realtime-optional architecture.

title: Rescope F001+F002 to local-fixture/emulator (no real jarvis-a6ee1 smoke) + correct allowed_paths
body: Pre-lock review at parent F003 dispatch time surfaced two internal inconsistencies in this plan's draft frontmatter. (1) child_charter.allowed_paths still pointed at `axiom/packages/dashboard/**`, `axiom/packages/sync/**`, `axiom/packages/functions/**` — predates D006's rename when the static dashboard moved to DontPanic/dashboard/ per plan 003 F007. Implementer would have been blocked from touching the actual target dir. FIXED: allowed_paths now `dashboard/**` + `scripts/firebase_adapter/**` + the plan dir. (2) F001 acceptance #4 required a smoke test against jarvis-a6ee1 with seed Firestore state — but parent_acceptance_item explicitly defers F003-F005 'until operator credentials in place'. Internal contradiction: F001#4 needed the very credentials parent_acceptance defers. FIXED: F001 acceptance #4 + F002 acceptance #5 + F002 description now target local Firebase emulator OR static-mock fixture; real jarvis-a6ee1 smoke deferred to F005. Plan target_project lowered from jarvis-a6ee1 → none for this session's scope. Plan body Acceptance Summary rewritten to match. Lock: status draft → active after rescope.

title: F003 Cloud Functions code shipped — deploy operator-gated
body: F003 implementer dispatch (target_env=dev, target_project=(none)) lands the three dashboard mutation callables under `dashboard/functions/` along with an MCP bridge, operator-role auth gate, kanban→status mapper, RUNBOOK with Tailscale Funnel walkthrough, and 39 smoke tests (4 vitest files). All 39 new tests + 356 prior dashboard tests pass (395/395). Per parent_acceptance_item / D007 the actual `firebase deploy --only functions` step stays operator-gated until `jarvis-a6ee1` credentials reactivate; this dispatch ships the code + tests against a stubbed MCP bridge so the deploy can run unattended once credentials land. firebase.json grew a `functions` block (codebase=dashboard-mutations, nodejs20) so the deploy invocation is wired.

title: F003 remains open after auditor rejection
body: Parallel dispatch triage repaired the ledger after the implementer flipped F003 to passes:true. The codex i1 auditor rejected close-out: deployment/callable acceptance was not satisfied, the evidence is stubbed rather than end-to-end, and the Cloud Function-to-MCP bridge still has unresolved architecture/API issues. The implementer code and audit artifacts remain useful partial evidence, but F003 is not complete. The feature acceptance text was restored to the locked deployed/callable/end-to-end boundary and F003 was reset to passes:false. D008 remains as the implementer claim, not the final operator verdict.

title: Pre-redispatch remediation: lazy MCP bridge closes auth-ordering defect
body: Triage found a real F003 defect: `dashboard/functions/index.js` created the MCP bridge before the handler-level Operator auth check, which meant an unauthenticated caller could trigger `MCP_TUNNEL_URL.value()` / `MCP_TUNNEL_TOKEN.value()` materialization before being rejected. The remediation adds `createLazyMcpBridge()` in `dashboard/functions/lib/mcp-bridge.js` and wires `index.js` to pass that lazy proxy into the callables. The callables still run `requireOperator` before any `bridge.call`, so tunnel config and secret access now happen only after auth passes. Verification: `npm --prefix dashboard/functions run lint` passes; focused dashboard functions suite passes 45 tests; full dashboard Vitest suite passes 409 tests. F003 remains passes:false because deploy and real end-to-end smoke are still unsatisfied.

title: Capability manifest boundary: Firebase realtime is adapter-only, static dashboard is core
body: ADR-001 and commit c3c2059 establish `capabilities/*.json` as the external capability manifest convention. This plan binds to `capabilities/firebase-dashboard.json`: DontPanic core owns state projection, bundled static dashboard export, MCP mutation tools, doctor profile hooks, and adapter governance; the Firebase adapter owns Firestore mirror schema, sync daemon, Firebase dashboard config, Cloud Functions, and Firestore rules; the operator owns the Firebase project, Auth, credentials, deploy, costs, and hosting choice. This reinforces the existing D006 split: static dashboard is core and must stay usable with no Firebase dependency; Firebase realtime is an optional adapter under `--profile firebase-dashboard`, never a default core onboarding blocker. Enforcement is aspirational until plan 2026-05-21-001-feat-capability-manifest-consumers-v0 lands its manifest loader/consumer features; until then this D-entry is a boundary citation for F003-F005 redispatch.

title: F004 completed: authenticated reads, client writes denied, rules deployed
body: F004 now implements the Firebase adapter boundary from D003 and D011. `firestore.rules` allows browser clients to read mirrored projection state only when `request.auth != null`; all client-side writes are denied with `allow write: if false`. Writes remain server-side through Admin SDK paths (sync daemon and Cloud Functions). Verification: focused rules test passes (3 tests), full dashboard suite passes (21 files / 412 tests), functions lint passes, and `firebase deploy --project jarvis-a6ee1 --only firestore:rules` released the rules to cloud.firestore. F003 remains passes:false because deployed callable functions and the Cloud Function -> MCP tunnel smoke are still unsatisfied; F005 remains blocked on F003.
